correctness.rationale: For t=d/b>1, positive predator observation forces x>t. The inverse equation H_Y(u) has strictly negative second derivative, tends to -infinity at both ends, and hence has exactly 0/1/2 positive roots according to a uniquely parameterized fold. The fold X=epsilon-rR_t(u), Y=(rb/(at))(2t-1+2u)u^2 is monotone in X. Exact integration yields A=(r^2b/(at))P_t(u*) and asymptotic b epsilon^3/(12atr(2t-1)). Uniform rescaling proves the limiting caustic and inverse branches. Exact symbolic identities, sample numerical inverse reconstruction and independent quadrature passed; the proof does not depend on finite experiments.

value.rationale: The smallest prey immigration capable of creating any strictly positive next-generation prey–predator observation is mathematically and biologically motivated when predator replacement requires prey above carrying capacity (d/b>1). The exact two-sheet region and its Lebesgue area quantify backward observational ambiguity, with a sharp nonzero cubic coefficient at onset. This is a natural continuous geometric invariant and complete classification, not a chosen arbitrary finite slice; its value does not rest on asserting long-term biological persistence.
